prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened in the parking lot?

A: I was pulling out of a space near the store entrance. It was a busy afternoon and the lot was crowded. I was backing out slowly, and I heard a horn, then felt the impact on the driver's side of my car.

Q: Had you checked your mirrors and looked behind you before you started backing?

A: I checked the mirror, but there was a delivery van parked at an angle that blocked part of my view. I didn't see the other car until it was almost on me.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle's speed or direction at all?

A: Not really. It seemed to be coming down the aisle fairly quickly, but I couldn't tell for sure.

Q: Were there any witnesses or photos taken at the scene?

A: A man in a red shirt stopped and asked if I was okay. I took a few photos of both cars with my phone before the tow truck came.

Q: Let's talk about your injury. What happened to your wrist?

A: When the car jolted, I put my right hand out to brace myself against the steering wheel and the dashboard. My wrist bent badly. I went to the emergency room later that day, and they said it was fractured.

Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since then?

A: Yes, I've seen an orthopedic doctor twice. I'm wearing a splint and I have physical therapy scheduled for next week.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add before we wrap up?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car repaired and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. We'll be in touch with next steps. Have a good day.

A: You too. Thanks.
